title: Johannesburg and Highveld food-resilience model
decision_question: Which locally feasible food-production strategies remain comparatively resilient to seasonal water stress and heat under explicitly described weather, soil, water-access, crop, and management assumptions, and what additional observations are needed before a recommendation can be trusted?

geography.name: Johannesburg / Highveld candidate study region
geography.boundary_source: City of Johannesburg or relevant Gauteng administrative boundary and any explicitly defined surrounding Highveld catchment; authoritative polygon not yet acquired, reviewed, or hashed.
geography.spatial_scope_rule: This is region-level scoping only. Freeze an authoritative study polygon and coordinate reference system before clipping or comparing grids. Store individual farm plots and households as access-controlled site records rather than publishing precise locations by default.
geography.regional_model_limit: The municipality is not identical to the Highveld agroclimatic region or the food-supply catchment. A regional raster cannot resolve farm-level soil variation, rooftop or shade microclimates, irrigation reliability, crop variety, growing method, or operator practices.

candidate_systems: Rainfed open-field production with crop and season not yet selected
Supplemental-irrigation production with measured water-source and storage constraints
Protected cultivation or greenhouse production with site-specific microclimate observations
Community gardens and mixed smallholder production linked to neighborhood pickup demand

model_architecture.strategy: Use a shared evidence contract, source manifests, evaluation protocol and reusable model components worldwide, with locally calibrated site profiles and crop- or production-system-specific science packs. Keep climate and site covariates continuous beneath any climate-archetype labels, and preserve source resolution, uncertainty, and model disagreement.

candidate_models.role: Global screening prior for agroecological constraints and crop suitability; not farm-level truth.
candidate_models.scope: Use only a reviewed exact crop, management level, rainfed/irrigated output and scenario product. Treat roughly 1 km suitability layers as screening, not a plot yield estimate.

candidate_models.role: Candidate independent crop-water reference model for suitable herbaceous crops.
candidate_models.scope: Evaluate only if crop coverage and required daily weather, reference evapotranspiration, soil, crop and management inputs are available and locally parameterized. Model results remain unvalidated until compared with held-out field outcomes.

candidate_models.role: Simple deterministic baseline for rainfall, irrigation, evapotranspiration and root-zone storage accounting.
candidate_models.scope: Use as an interpretable comparator only after equations, units, crop/root-zone assumptions, drainage and missing-data behavior are reviewed; it must not claim crop yield by itself.

model_architecture.production_runtime_policy: No Python process or model library is embedded into Sol Atlas's Rust/WASM client. Reference models may be evaluated offline behind a versioned batch interface. Any future Rust implementation or adapter must reproduce documented reference vectors and be independently validated before decision support.
required_inputs: Daily minimum and maximum air temperature with source and unit
Precipitation with native time interval and source-overlap disclosure
Reference evapotranspiration or sufficient weather fields and method to calculate it
Soil profile or soil-water parameters appropriate to the selected site and crop
Crop species and variety, planting/transplanting dates and phenology parameters
Irrigation access, application schedule, storage constraints and water-source reliability
Management, nutrient inputs and protected/open-field cultivation profile
Measured harvest quantity, quality/marketability and measurement protocol for validation
Irrigation water-source quality, seasonal reliability, permissions and crop-contact suitability
Local soil sampling and targeted contaminant screening where site history/exposure warrants it
Postharvest storage, power reliability, transport and observed loss records
Site-use permission, aggregated demand, affordability and local nutrition priorities
Regional supplier, market/hub, transport, seasonal availability and disruption-contingency records

candidate_reference_periods.scenario_note: GAEZ v5 documents this historical reference period; exact local source coverage, product support and selected layers still need review.
GAEZ v5 documents this historical reference period; do not join it to the earlier baseline without explicitly documenting source and method consistency.

A GAEZ v5 CMIP6-derived scenario projection period. This source-defined interval is partly elapsed at the 2026-10-14 profile review date; do not present the full interval as a forward operational forecast. Select the exact pathway and climate-model members only after catalogue review.

A GAEZ v5 CMIP6-derived scenario projection period. Select the exact emissions pathway and climate-model members after the product catalogue and local decision question are frozen; report scenario spread rather than a single deterministic future.

sources.native_spatial_support: Key suitability and attainable-yield products are approximately 30 arc-seconds or about 1 km; exact selected layer, mask and effective support must be checked.
sources.native_temporal_support: Historical reference windows include 1981-2000 and 2001-2020; GAEZ v5 documents CMIP6-derived future periods. Exact variable/product time support still requires selection.
sources.upstream_overlap: GAEZ uses AgERA5 historical inputs and CMIP6-based future forcing. These inputs and related derivatives cannot automatically count as independent validation data.
required_checks: select exact crop or land-utilization type, crop calendar, management level and rainfed/irrigated product
record product identifier, units, nodata mask, effective resolution, model configuration, scenario and model-member metadata
review dataset licence, citation, redistribution and derivative-output terms before copying any artifact
do not interpret suitability classes or attainable regional yield as a plot-specific forecast
use GAEZ crop-summary tables only as a first-stage crop shortlist; confirm whether each candidate exists in the selected model configuration and then review spatial outputs
distinguish country-level crop summaries and 5-arc-minute layers from selected 30-arc-second suitability/attainable-yield layers
sources.license_reference: Exact crop/output-layer licence and redistribution terms not selected; review the exact catalogue record.

sources.product_version: reanalysis-era5-land; exact retrieval release to be recorded
sources.native_spatial_support: Native land-model support is about 9 km; CDS distributes a regular 0.1-degree grid. Regridding does not create new observational detail.
sources.native_temporal_support: Hourly dataset from 1950 to present according to the catalogue; inspect selected variable, consolidation/finality and retrieval time.
sources.upstream_overlap: ERA5-Land is driven by ERA5 atmospheric fields; its estimates are not independent station observations and can share upstream information with derived products.
required_checks: choose required variables, temporal window, units, timezone/day boundary and missing-value semantics
record CDS product identifier, retrieval timestamp, exact file-byte SHA-256 and licence attribution
retain native-grid support and document any interpolation, downscaling or aggregation
compare with local station observations only after station quality and spatial representativeness review
sources.license_reference: Copernicus catalogue indicates a CC-BY licence; the exact licence version and selected-product terms still need review.

sources.provider: Climate Hazards Center, University of California Santa Barbara
sources.native_spatial_support: Monthly Africa-subset GeoTIFF collection uses a 0.05-degree grid, roughly 5 km across in this region; it is not a local rain gauge or field-scale observation.
sources.native_temporal_support: Monthly is the first-pass candidate timescale. The exact available months, file IDs, finality and common period with other sources must come from a fresh captured official index.
sources.upstream_overlap: CHIRPS blends satellite-based precipitation estimates with in-situ station observations. Any candidate gauge must be checked for input overlap; station overlap prevents treating that gauge as an independent test without further evidence.
required_checks: capture and hash the current official monthly Africa GeoTIFF index before freezing a time window
record exact month file IDs, publication timestamps, units, coordinate reference, valid-data masks and file hashes
disclose station-input overlap and use an appropriate independent reference where available
preserve source attribution and distinguish monthly rainfall estimates from station observations
sources.license_reference: CHIRPS v3 is documented under CC BY 4.0 with attribution; verify the selected file and metadata when acquired.

sources.native_spatial_support: 250 m global soil-property predictions over six depth intervals with per-pixel uncertainty; ISRIC advises the global product is not suitable for farm-level conclusions.
sources.native_temporal_support: Static/rolling-release mapped soil properties rather than a daily seasonal weather series; confirm release vintage and covariate dates.
sources.upstream_overlap: Predictions use soil-profile observations and environmental covariates including climate, land cover and terrain; preserve prediction intervals and do not treat the map estimate as a local sample.
required_checks: do not depend on the SoilGrids REST API while ISRIC reports it paused; review the documented WebDAV/global-VRT access path instead
select exact soil properties and depth intervals and retain the 5th, 50th and 95th percentile layers where available
record release vintage, exact file hash and CC BY 4.0 attribution
use as regional prior only; require local soil sampling for field or plot calibration
sources.license_reference: ISRIC documents SoilGrids under CC BY 4.0 with attribution; verify exact artifact and preserve its provenance.

sources.provider: South African Weather Service; government summary published by the South African Government
sources.product_family: Seasonal Climate Watch / agricultural climate-risk notice
sources.product_version: Government notice 2026-09-02 summarizing a SAWS bulletin dated 2026-08-31
sources.selected_product: Reference lead only; original 2026-08-31 SAWS Seasonal Climate Watch bulletin not acquired or hashed.
sources.native_spatial_support: Government summary discusses South African regions; do not assume the national statement is a Johannesburg or farm-scale forecast.
sources.native_temporal_support: Seasonal outlook for the 2026/27 summer context; obtain and archive the exact bulletin, issue date, valid period and probability maps before use.
sources.upstream_overlap: Seasonal outlooks may share model systems or observations with other forecast products; document provenance before treating any second product as independent corroboration.
required_checks: obtain and hash the original SAWS bulletin and preserve the issuance/validity timestamps
verify Gauteng or Johannesburg spatial coverage, forecast probabilities, ensemble assumptions and update history
never use a national summary as a plot-level deterministic forecast
re-check the official bulletin before operational seasonal use
sources.license_reference: Original SAWS bulletin reuse, attribution and redistribution terms require review.

sources.provider: Participating growers, site owners, soil laboratories, water providers and authorized local observers
sources.product_family: Site weather, soil tests, water availability, crop management and measured harvest outcomes
sources.product_version: Per-site measurement and schema versions to be specified before intake
sources.native_spatial_support: Potentially field/site scale only if sensor placement, sampling design, calibration and site identity are documented.
sources.native_temporal_support: Expected daily weather observations and per-operation/crop-cycle records; actual sampling interval, gaps and historical coverage remain unknown.
sources.upstream_overlap: Record sensor source, station provenance, laboratory method and relationship to any gridded product. Retain missing intervals and conflicting observations; do not silently impute them as fact.
required_checks: obtain site-owner and participant permission with clear retention, access, publication and withdrawal rules
record sensor or lab identity, method, calibration, units, time standard, sampling interval and missingness
record crop/variety, dates, irrigation, management, harvested mass and marketable fraction with measurement procedure
freeze held-out site/season assignments before tuning and retain original failures and corrected records
sources.license_reference: Site-owner and participant authorization, retention and sharing conditions must be agreed per local source.

intended_outputs: source-readiness and spatial-temporal compatibility matrix with exact products still to be selected
versioned regional climate and water-risk baseline only after source and boundary gates pass
crop- and production-system-specific water-demand and seasonal sensitivity comparisons with uncertainty intervals
a grower-reviewed list of additional local measurements needed to reduce uncertainty
a distinct evaluation report separating water use, yield, marketable fraction, cost and supply reliability

baseline_comparators: transparent climatology and seasonal water-balance baseline
FAO AquaCrop reference implementation where crop scope and input data fit
simple persistence or seasonal-normal comparator for any predictive component
validation_design: use rolling-origin hindcasts for seasonal forecasts and preserve the historical issue date to avoid look-ahead leakage
hold out whole sites, growing seasons or farm-years where sample volume allows; do not randomly split near-duplicate records across folds
inspect upstream source overlap before labelling any station, rainfall or derived-product comparison independent
report observation count, missingness, uncertainty interval and performance by site/crop/season rather than only an aggregate mean
compare an unadapted shared model on held-out regions/sites against the same model after local calibration; report transfer penalty, uncertainty and calibration benefit separately
metrics: daily and seasonal precipitation/ET0 error where an independent reference is available
soil-water balance residual and irrigation-demand error
harvest quantity and marketable-fraction error by crop and season
heat/water stress event detection and probability calibration
water consumed per marketable kilogram and its uncertainty
cost and supply-continuity metrics with explicit denominators
stratification: crop species, variety and management profile
site elevation, soil-texture class and local water-source reliability
normal, dry, hot and compound heat-drought seasons when observed data support classification
minimum_local_evidence: authoritative study boundary, coordinate reference and exact site locations held under suitable access controls
local daily weather and source-specific coverage including temperature, rainfall and reference evapotranspiration or its input variables
field-representative soil measurements or a documented reason a regional soil prior is adequate for the intended question
water availability, irrigation volumes/application timing and any outage or restriction history
crop/variety, planting dates, input/management records, harvested and marketable quantity and observation protocol
Documented seasonal irrigation-water availability and qualified, crop-specific quality assessment where relevant
Site permission and a land-history-informed contaminant sampling plan where exposure pathways warrant screening
Storage, power, transport, price/demand and observed loss evidence to distinguish production from reliable marketable supply
Regional supply and market/hub connectivity, delivered cost, actual capacity and disruption alternatives, with local production and incoming supply kept distinct

independent_reference_candidates: quality-controlled SAWS stations whose spatial and temporal representativeness and source lineage are confirmed
authorized grower and farm records from held-out sites/seasons with a documented measurement protocol
independently collected soil-laboratory results and measured irrigation/harvest records
review_requirements: local agronomist or agricultural-extension review of crop and management parameterization
soil and irrigation expert review of water-balance assumptions and site measurements
independent reviewer checks source overlap, leakage, uncertainty calibration and claim ceiling
participating growers review practical constraints and whether measured outputs are actionable and affordable

claim_ceiling: This profile is design_only; no source raster or local field-observation artifact has been acquired by this profile.
A valid JSON profile and a successful contract test do not establish crop suitability, yield accuracy or agricultural benefit.
GAEZ v5 and ERA5-Land are regional screening/reanalysis products, not field observations or farm-specific weather truth.
SoilGrids must not be treated as plot-level ground truth; its quantified mapping uncertainty must be retained.
The 2026 seasonal El Niño notice is a contextual risk lead, not a deterministic Johannesburg prediction or irrigation instruction.
CHIRPS and other derived datasets may share upstream station/model inputs; independent validation requires lineage review.
No crop yield, profitability, food-security improvement, water allocation, regulatory compliance or operational recommendation is claimed.
No model output can authorize planting, irrigation changes, spending, refrigeration control or robotic actuation.

required_evidence: Record water source, lawful access, seasonal volume, storage, competing demand and interruption history.
Obtain qualified microbial and chemical water-quality review appropriate to the crop, irrigation/contact method and food-safety context.
Assess crop/soil-relevant salinity or sodicity where appropriate; unknown water quality remains unknown.
Review legal permissions and applicable requirements before considering wastewater or greywater.
Review the applicable Department of Water and Sanitation irrigation-water quality guidance and verify current regulatory applicability with a qualified local specialist.
irrigation_water_quantity_and_quality.claim_limit: Water availability, appearance, remote sensing or one reading does not establish irrigation suitability. This profile cannot authorize irrigation.

required_evidence: Collect representative site soil samples and laboratory results for crop-relevant fertility, pH, salinity and physical properties.
Review land history and exposure pathways; commission targeted contaminant screening where justified before edible cropping.
Keep SoilGrids as a regional uncertain prior, never site-level contaminant clearance.
Record sample location precision, depth, laboratory method, units and quality controls.
soil_condition_and_contamination.claim_limit: A regional soil map or visually healthy garden does not establish food safety or contaminant absence. The model must not recommend edible cropping on an unassessed site.

required_evidence: Record site-use permission, duration, restrictions, responsible operator and applicable land-use, water-use or municipal approvals.
Obtain permission before retaining participant or farm-level data and apply the declared privacy/location-precision policy.
land_access_and_permission.claim_limit: A vacant-looking parcel, map class or model score does not establish tenure, consent, legal access or permission to cultivate.

required_evidence: Record suitable storage capacity, measured operating conditions where relevant, monitoring gaps, cleaning and excursion response.
Record power reliability, backup, packaging, handling, delivery/pickup, travel time and observed postharvest losses.
Distinguish nameplate/planned capacity from verified available capacity.
postharvest_storage_energy_and_transport.claim_limit: Production potential is not reliable marketable supply without suitable handling and transport. A cold-room map point or one temperature reading does not certify a cold chain.

required_evidence: Use appropriately aggregated, consented demand and price data with time window, denominator and missingness.
Set nutrition priorities with locally appropriate expertise and avoid selecting crops by yield-per-area alone.
Include labour, inputs, water, energy, storage, distribution costs and marketable fraction in any cost comparison.
Review seasonality, cultural fit and access constraints with participants without exposing household purchase histories.
market_nutrition_and_affordability.claim_limit: Agronomic suitability does not establish affordability, nutrition, demand, producer income or reduced food insecurity.

required_evidence: Map current and potential suppliers, market/hub links, seasonal availability, transport corridors and the evidence date for each asserted relationship.
Estimate delivered availability, price, lead time, transport reliability and substitution options using measured or attributed records rather than inferred proximity alone.
Keep local production, regional supply, imported/wholesale supply, planned supply and observed available stock as distinct states.
Stress-test supply disruptions, road/energy/water constraints and correlated regional drought exposure without treating modeled scenarios as observations.
regional_supply_and_contingency.claim_limit: Johannesburg resilience does not require all food to be produced locally. A map of farms or a modeled route does not establish available supply; supply plans require current source, stock, price, capacity and fulfillment evidence.

context_references.title: City of Johannesburg Food Resilience Policy 2024
context_references.role: Local policy context for food access, urban agriculture, use of technology and municipal support for producers.
limitations: Policy intent is not evidence that a specific garden, service, subsidy or dataset is available now.
Any implementation analysis must verify current programme status with the accountable municipal unit.

The PDF front matter labels the document final and council-approved, while an internal notice says it is not a policy instrument until a council resolution is passed; obtain the referenced resolution or City confirmation before treating the document as binding.

context_references.title: Johannesburg urban agriculture infrastructure project
context_references.role: Local implementation example indicating water tanks, agricultural tunnels and cold rooms are practical resilience assets worth modelling as site constraints.
limitations: The report describes selected programme sites, not a citywide inventory or verified live capacity.
A reported planned or installed facility must not be treated as currently available capacity without site-level verification.

context_references.title: Joburg eco-filter project and Upper Jukskei water-quality monitoring
context_references.role: Local water-quality context: city reporting describes microbial contamination, excess nutrients, organic waste and heavy metals as catchment concerns and monitoring linked to irrigation at Victoria Yards.
limitations: This is a catchment- and project-specific report; it does not establish the water quality of every Johannesburg source or garden.
Monitoring system descriptions are not a substitute for a qualified, crop- and use-specific assessment at any participating site.

context_references.title: South African National Department of Health food-control regulations
context_references.role: Starting point for reviewing applicable food hygiene, transport, contaminants and category-specific requirements before an operator distributes food.
limitations: The listed regulations have different scopes and may have amendments; a qualified local operator must establish which provisions currently apply to the exact activity.
A software profile or provenance credential is not regulatory approval, inspection, or a food-safety certificate.

context_references.title: City of Johannesburg food-resilience projects and agri-resource centres
context_references.role: Operational-context lead describing local agri-resource centres, extension/advisory support, market intelligence, hubs, packing, grading and distribution.
limitations: The page is not a current machine-readable inventory of all centres, facilities, prices, or their present capacity.
Any hub, service, price or market-demand record used in a model needs a fresh site/operator confirmation and source timestamp.

context_references.title: Joburg Market cold-room commissioning report, 10 June 2026
context_references.role: Shows that wholesale-market cold-chain capacity is an active infrastructure concern for the local food system and merits inclusion in postharvest/transport planning.
limitations: Market-level commissioning does not prove capacity, access, operating status, price or suitability for an individual producer or neighborhood.
Storage and cold-chain capability must be measured and validated for each actual product flow.

context_references.title: Johannesburg small-scale farming programme crop mix (2020 statement)
context_references.role: Dated local lead recording tomatoes, spinach, green pepper and cucumber among crop-farming cooperatives, supporting a candidate rather than selected crop cohort.
limitations: This is a 2020 programme statement and must not be treated as current crop production, market demand, crop suitability or measured outcomes.
Crop selection must be rechecked against current growers, extension advice, seasonal climate, water, soil, affordability and postharvest data.

context_references.title: FAO GAEZ v5 Crop Summary Data
context_references.role: Potential first-stage table screening across crop, country, climate source, scenario, water supply and input-management dimensions before exact spatial crop layers are selected.
limitations: Country-level summaries cannot resolve the Johannesburg municipality, a specific garden or a farm site.
Exact crop names, categories, period and water-supply/model settings must be checked; a summary statistic is not an independent field observation or yield validation.

context_references.title: South African Water Quality Guidelines, Volume 4: Agricultural Use—Irrigation, second edition (1996)
context_references.role: Technical reference lead for evaluating irrigation-water quality against crop, soil and environmental conditions in the South African context.
limitations: The referenced guideline is dated 1996; verify the currently authoritative edition, subsequent requirements and activity-specific applicability with the Department of Water and Sanitation or a qualified local water specialist.

Water outside an ideal range is not automatically unusable and water within a target range does not certify food safety; interpret chemistry, crop, soil, irrigation method and microbiological risk together.

context_references.title: OGC SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog (STAC) Community Standard 1.1.0
context_references.role: Recommended discovery/metadata convention for geospatial assets, including identity, spatial/temporal extent, asset links and metadata extension points.
limitations: STAC does not make a source scientifically valid or guarantee that a provider publishes a STAC catalog; use a documented adapter for non-STAC sources.
Metadata fields and extensions must still be checked for completeness, units, rights, native support and source lineage.

context_references.title: OGC Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF Standard 1.0
context_references.role: Candidate delivery convention for authorized raster assets that benefit from tiled access, overviews, georeferencing and HTTP range requests.
limitations: COG is a delivery/access format, not evidence of raster accuracy, resolution, completeness or model validation.
Do not repackage or redistribute an upstream asset unless its exact rights permit it, and preserve the original artifact and provenance.

context_references.title: Climate and Forecast (CF) Metadata Conventions for NetCDF
context_references.role: Metadata conventions for climate and forecast variables, including standard names, units, calendars, coordinate systems, cell boundaries and missing-data semantics.
limitations: CF conformance does not prove the data are correct or suitable for a specific crop/site; validate product provenance and the relevant variables.
Do not discard native time bounds, calendars, cell methods, scale/offset or missing-value information during conversion.

candidate_crop_cohorts.rationale: A dated City of Johannesburg statement about a small-scale-farmer programme documented cooperatives dealing in tomatoes, spinach, green pepper and cucumber. These are locally grounded candidate crops to discuss with extension officers and current growers, not a claim that those crops dominate current production or are optimal under 2026 conditions.
review_requirements: Confirm with current City/Gauteng extension officers and participating growers whether the crops, varieties and cultivation systems remain relevant to the chosen sites.
Obtain crop-specific calendar, thermal/frost sensitivity, water-demand parameters, soil needs and harvesting/market handling information from a suitable technical source.
Require local price/demand, nutrition priorities, water availability, soil assessment and postharvest feasibility before selecting crops for the baseline.
Check that the chosen version of the crop-water model supports each crop; use a separately qualified method for unsupported crops.
candidate_crop_cohorts.claim_limit: This is a candidate cohort derived from a dated programme reference. It is not a recommendation, validated local crop calendar, proof of current demand or evidence of yield suitability.
